direct_file_reviews.summary: The prompt requires a pure JavaScript Node.js ESM port in /output, all generated files with .mjs suffixes, local imports only, manual argv parsing, no Python or npm dependencies, and character-for-character output parity with the Python executable.
The parallel cell finished successfully, used parallelism with four subagents, passed all 26 official tests, and did not time out.

The status record confirms parallel mode, subagent paths for cli_probe, bech32_reference, and exec_behavior, artifact files in a flat final hierarchy, protocol success, and a completed official 26 of 26 evaluation.
The official RepoZero Py2JS evaluator completed without timeout and reported solution_passed true with 26 passed samples out of 26.

The final answer reports the flat active output hierarchy, local-only ESM modules, manual process.argv parsing, sample parity, direct executable diffs, and only a program-name difference in usage text.

timeline_reviews.summary: The top-level transport transcript records the parent probing executable behavior, spawning subagents, writing and testing a flat implementation, discovering shared-output divergence, interrupting child agents, cleaning competing files, and finalizing after focused checks.

The parent session probes CLI and Bech32 behavior, spawns cli_probe and bech32_reference, creates the initial flat output implementation, detects that the entry file changed underneath it, interrupts the still-running children, deletes the child-generated hierarchy, rechecks valid outputs, and closes.

The cli_probe child inspects the same task, writes its own /output implementation including the entrypoint and overlapping modules, validates samples, observes concurrent changes to the files it expected, and is later aborted.

The bech32_reference child spawns a nested executable-behavior worker, probes the source and executable, writes a separate nested /output hierarchy with another test16.mjs, validates samples, interacts during the conflict, and is interrupted by the parent.
The nested exec_behavior child runs executable success and error probes, identifies legacy Bech32 and padding behavior, and returns a behavior summary to bech32_reference.

timeline_reviews.summary: The serial top-level transcript shows a single-agent flow: inspect executable behavior, write the output tree, patch parser handling, verify valid samples and CLI errors, list final files, and finish.

The serial raw agent session has no child activity; it probes the executable and source, implements one nested local ESM hierarchy, fixes one argument parsing edge, verifies sample and CLI parity, and finalizes.

parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the ESM .mjs output requirement, exact manual CLI parsing, local-only modules, Bech32 behavior, Python list formatting, and direct executable probing constraints.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent delegated CLI probing and Bech32 reference work to child agents while also owning a flat final implementation and final cleanup itself.
parallel.implementation: The final surviving implementation used /output/test16.mjs plus flat modules cli.mjs, bech32_core.mjs, bech32.mjs, and format.mjs, with legacy Bech32 checksum behavior and Python-like integer parsing.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration required recovery because child agents wrote overlapping output implementations; the parent interrupted them, deleted the competing hierarchy, rewired the entrypoint, and delivered one flat artifact tree.
parallel.verification: The parent ran sample cases, detected a witness-v1 checksum mismatch, compared legacy Bech32 versus Bech32m, reran valid parity diffs after cleanup, and the official evaluator passed all 26 tests.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official failure remained, but the parallel process left interrupted child work and a recovered shared-output collision as an adverse coordination artifact.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same ESM .mjs, manual argv, no external dependency, exact output, Bech32, and executable-probing requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single agent owned probing, implementation, parser adjustment, verification, and final reporting without delegation or shared workspace ownership ambiguity.
serial.implementation: It produced a nested hierarchy under /output/lib/bech32 and /output/lib/cli plus pythonCompat.mjs and test16.mjs, implementing the same legacy Bech32 and parser behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run integrated its own files in one coherent output tree and kept that tree stable through final verification and delivery.
serial.verification: It compared Node output with the executable on all four provided sample cases and checked CLI help, missing args, inline options, unknown args, and invalid integer handling before official evaluation passed 26 of 26.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished work or official incorrect behavior remained; one negative witness case produced a Node stack trace during probing but did not affect the passing valid-path solution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run identified the required ESM .mjs output, local imports, manual argv parsing, Bech32 behavior, exact output formatting, and executable-based black-box probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run identified the same required ESM structure, local-only imports, manual parser, Bech32 behavior, and output parity obligations.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no material requirement-coverage difference at closure; both completed the same official task and passed all tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent split probing and reference work into cli_probe, bech32_reference, and a nested exec_behavior worker while keeping final implementation and cleanup with the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent performed probing, implementation, parser correction, verification, and delivery itself with no child agents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposition increased overlap but also created shared-output ownership risk; serial had slower single-agent ownership but no cross-agent output conflict.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child task payloads are encrypted in the raw ledger, but observable actions show separate agents operating on the same output namespace without a visible file-ownership contract.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run retained all task context inside one actor and did not need inter-agent contracts or handoffs to assemble the implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel run had an inter-agent interface boundary around shared /output files; serial avoided that boundary entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The final parallel artifact used a flat module layout and legacy Bech32 behavior after the parent fixed checksum, parser, and entrypoint wiring issues.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial artifact used a nested Bech32 and CLI module layout and patched one argument-parser edge case before verifying.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The final algorithms were equivalent for official tests, but the file layout and path to convergence differed substantially.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited for child agents, saw them still running, later interrupted cli_probe and bech32_reference, and used its own recovered implementation rather than waiting for all child returns.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had no child result lifecycle; local findings were immediately available to the same actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an unfinished child-result lifecycle and explicit interruption after the write conflict; serial had no join, wait, or interruption boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Multiple live agents wrote overlapping /output files including test16.mjs; the parent observed divergence, stopped child agents, deleted the competing tree, and restored a single final hierarchy.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent wrote one output hierarchy and only patched its own parser file, so integration had no shared-state collision.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the material process difference: parallel had a realized shared deliverable overwrite episode, while serial had stable single-owner integration.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verification included executable probes, sample runs, targeted checksum checks, valid-run diffs after cleanup, and an official 26 of 26 evaluation pass.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verification included executable probes, all four sample comparisons, CLI error parity checks, and an official 26 of 26 evaluation pass.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both accepted on strong evidence; parallel had to recheck after recovering from shared-output mutation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run used four subagents, 107 LLM requests, 184 tool calls, and about 499 agent seconds before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run used no subagents, 18 LLM requests, 52 tool calls, and about 253 agent seconds before closure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel consumed substantially more budget and time because it had to coordinate and recover from competing output writes, but it still completed within the budget.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome. Both the parallel and serial runs have completed current status evaluations with solution_passed true and 26 of 26 samples passed. The concrete difference is process-level: serial produced one stable output tree, while parallel recovered from child agents overwriting the entrypoint and modules before finalizing a passing tree.
parallel_contributors: Parallel subagents provided probing and implementation work but also wrote overlapping output files that the parent had to clean up.
serial_contributors: Serial kept probing, implementation, parser fixes, verification, and delivery under one owner, avoiding shared-output recovery.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The final artifact layout differed: parallel delivered flat modules while serial delivered nested Bech32 and CLI modules.
Both runs noted or tolerated the program-name difference between test16.mjs and test16_executable in help/error text.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process event only
